_about: Why each class and relation exists, and who confirmed it. Written by the ontology interview and edited by hand. `validated_by` is empty until a person who knows the domain has actually confirmed the entry; leave it empty rather than guessing.

Assessment.question: What evidence supports the decision on quantum or damage?
Assessment.why: An estimate or expert opinion has its own author and date, and a decision must be able to cite it.

Claim.question: What is being asked for, under which policy, and what state is it in?
Claim.why: The claim is the unit of work and the unit of reporting, and it exists from first notice until closure.

Coverage.alternatives: Considered an attribute of Policy; rejected because a payment must point at exactly one coverage.
Coverage.question: Which coverage is this claim being paid under, and what limit applies?
Coverage.why: Limits, deductibles and exclusions attach to a coverage rather than a policy, and payments are charged against one.

Decision.alternatives: Considered a status field on Claim; rejected because a status keeps no reason and no history.
Decision.question: What was determined, when, and on what basis?
Decision.why: A determination has a date, a reason, evidence it relied on, and it can be superseded by a later one.

Document.question: Where is this written down?
Document.why: Every fact needs a source that can be checked, and the source is a file with its own date.

Endorsement.alternatives: Considered editing the Policy in place; rejected because it destroys the answer to what was in force on the loss date.
Endorsement.question: What changed on this policy, and from when?
Endorsement.why: A mid-term change alters cover for part of the period only, so it needs its own dates and its own source.

Incident.alternatives: Considered attributes on Claim; rejected because it makes catastrophe and aggregation questions unanswerable.
Incident.question: What actually happened, and how many claims came out of it?
Incident.why: One event can produce several claims, and it happens before any of them is reported, so it needs its own date.

Party.alternatives: Deliberately broad for a first draft. Split it as soon as you can name the sub-kinds you actually query.
Party.question: Who is involved, and in what capacity?
Party.why: Policyholder, claimant, third party, witness, repairer and provider all need to be referenced, and the same person can be more than one.

Payment.question: What has been paid out, to whom, and against which coverage?
Payment.why: Each payment is charged to a coverage and made to a party, and the total is a question about many of them.

Policy.alternatives: Considered folding into Claim; rejected because one policy carries many claims and its terms change independently.
Policy.question: Which policy was in force when this loss happened?
Policy.why: Cover is decided against a policy at a moment in time, so the policy must be a thing with a period, not a field on a claim.

Procedure.question: How are we supposed to handle this?
Procedure.why: The documented way of working is what handling is measured against, and it changes over time.

Recovery.alternatives: Considered a negative Payment; rejected because subrogation and salvage have different parties and different reasons.
Recovery.question: What came back in, and from whom?
Recovery.why: Net cost is a question about money in and money out, and a model with only payments cannot answer it.

Regulation.question: What external rule constrains how we handle this?
Regulation.why: An external rule has a source outside the organization and cannot be changed by it, which makes it a different kind of thing from a procedure.

Role.alternatives: Considered pointing tasks straight at a Party; rejected because it breaks when someone leaves.
Role.question: Who is accountable for handling this, without naming a person?
Role.why: Handling authority and workload attach to a function, and the person filling it changes while the history must stay correct.

Task.question: What still has to happen on this claim, and who owns it?
Task.why: Handling is a sequence of committed pieces of work with owners and states, which an attribute cannot carry.

Vehicle.question: Which vehicle was involved, and what has been claimed on it before?
Vehicle.why: A vehicle outlives any single policy or claim, so history attaches to it rather than to either.

part_of_claim.alternatives: Considered a separate relation per item type; rejected because every consumer would then need to know all five.
part_of_claim.question: Show me everything on this claim.
part_of_claim.why: One relation gathers tasks, assessments, decisions, payments and recoveries onto a claim, so the claim view is a single traversal.

supersedes.alternatives: Considered overwriting; rejected because it destroys the answer to what we believed at the time.
supersedes.question: What did this replace, and what was true before?
supersedes.why: Correction by supersession keeps the old fact queryable and dated, which is what makes an audit possible.

performs.question: Who carries out this procedure?
performs.why: Procedure documents say which role does the work; without the relation the answer lives only in prose and cannot be traversed. Found on the first real run: both a hand-written proposal and an agent's proposal needed it.
performs.alternatives: Considered going through Task (a task follows a procedure and is assigned to a role); rejected because a procedure's owner is a standing fact, not a property of each task.
